extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, inventors, and patent-office practitioners (historical U.S./U.K. patent practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and legal rules for drafting patent specifications, filing caveats/petitions, taking required oaths/payments, and procedures for reissue/renewal and corrections before the patent office. Focused on what must be disclosed, formal requirements, and agency discretion under 19th-century statutes cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full description of every new part
rubrics_metrics.description: Every part which is new, however minute, must be clearly described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In specifications of manufactures, principles carried into practice, and combinations, every new element must be set forth distinctly so the public obtains the invention as the patentee enjoys it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification content for chemical substances
rubrics_metrics.description: When a chemical discovery is the foundation of the invention, the substance produced (not the principle or process) ought to be described.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the ingredients, their proportions, the time of mixing, &c., fully, and then the beneficial use to which the substance can be applied. (Cited: Turner v. Winter.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification content for machines and manufactures
rubrics_metrics.description: In descriptions of machines there must be set forth the cheapest materials, the most exact proportions of the parts, the most expeditious and the best mode of conducting them, with the precise times of putting on or taking off any part of the machine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An improvement or new combination must be kept distinctly apart from the old manufacture; disclose best modes of making and using the machine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enablement / adequate public disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: The public must be put in possession of the manufacture in a way as ample and beneficial as the patentee enjoys it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A method, if claimed, must be described so clearly and evidently that no experiments are necessary to learn it and put it into practice as beneficially as the patentee enjoys it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat content and filing procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A caveat for an incomplete invention must set forth the design and purpose thereof, and its principal and distinguishing characteristics, and is filed on payment of twenty dollars and preserved in secrecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another application that may interfere is made within one year, the commissioner shall deposit the description/specifications/drawings/model in confidential archives and mail notice to the caveat filer, who then has three months to file his description/specifications/drawings/model; if specifications of claim interfere, like proceedings follow as in interfering applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of petition / application in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Application for a patent must be made in writing (historically by petition) to the Commissioner of Patents; the form is not material provided it sets forth the facts required for the oath.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filed, the petition is presumed to adopt the specification filed with it and to ask for a patent for the invention described; Patent Office rules give advisable petition forms (see Appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath / affirmation of original inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must make oath or affirmation that he does verily believe he is the original and first inventor (and that he does not know or believe the same was ever before known or used) and state his citizenship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The oath need only be a belief (not actual knowledge). An irregularity in the form of the oath may be cured by issuing the patent; in some holdings a patent may be valid even if oath not taken. When the oath is recited in the patent it forms the foundation of the onus probandi on a challenger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fees before consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any application is considered by the commissioner, the applicant must pay required fees: historically $30 for U.S. citizens/resident aliens and $500 for subjects of the King of Great Britain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory fee amounts are cited in the Act of July 4, 1836, §9 (historical figures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatures and corrections to issued patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents are to be issued in the name of the United States, under the seal, signed by the Secretary of State and countersigned by the Commissioner of Patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanction of the Secretary of State to correct a clerical mistake may be given in writing afterwards; the Commissioner may correct clerical mistakes without re-signing; if the mistake is in the enrolled patent and material, corrections may only operate prospectively; clerical corrections may operate back to original date except as to third persons with intervening rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimer / memorandum of alteration under 5 & 6 Wm. IV c.83
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantee may enter with the clerk of patents a disclaimer of any part of the title or specification stating the reason, or enter a memorandum of any alteration not extending the exclusive right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such disclaimer/alteration requires leave (fiat) of attorney-general/solicitor-general or lord-advocate respectively; caveats may be entered against disclaimers/alterations and give notice rights; disclaimers/alterations generally are not receivable in evidence in pending suits (except scire facias); the executive may require advertisement of the disclaimer/alteration prior to fiat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and procedure for reissue / renewal of patent (defective/insufficient specification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a patent is inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective or insufficient description or specification, or by claiming more than the inventor had a right to claim as new, and the error arose by inadvertence/accident/mistake without fraudulent intention, the Commissioner may, upon surrender of the patent and payment of fifteen dollars, cause a new patent to be issued for the same invention for the residue of the original term in accordance with the corrected description and specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of death or assignment, executors/assignees have similar rights. The reissued patent and corrected specification have the same legal effect for actions subsequently arising as though originally filed in corrected form. The patentee may also annex descriptions of newly-invented improvements by like proceedings and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision/restriction of claims on reissue or addition of improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: When application is made for addition of a newly-discovered improvement or for correction and reissue, the specification of claim annexed to every such patent shall be subject to revision and restriction in the same manner as original applications; the Commissioner shall not add improvements nor grant reissue until the applicant has entered a disclaimer or altered his specification of claim in accordance with the Commissioner's decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dissatisfied with the Commissioner's decision, the applicant has the same remedies and privileges as in original patent-application proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference to Commissioner; finality of reissue decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the Commissioner in respect to surrendering an old patent and granting a new one is not reexaminable elsewhere unless it appears on the face of the patent that he exceeded his authority, or the new one was obtained by collusion between Commissioner and patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prima facie the renewed patent is for the same invention as the old; the Commissioner is the appropriate initial judge of facts and law regarding sufficiency, excess claims, and inadvertence; his bona fide decision is generally conclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of claims on reissued patents (no obligation to claim everything originally claimed)
rubrics_metrics.description: On reissue the patentee is not required to claim in the renewed patent all things which were claimed in the original patent; he may omit parts and retain what he deems proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutes and case law permit restricting or altering claims on reissue if original claims were excessive; the Commissioner may require disclaimers or alterations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of reissued patent on term and assignees
rubrics_metrics.description: When a patent is renewed (reissued) it is granted for the unexpired term commencing from the date of the original patent surrendered, and operates from the commencement of the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reissued patent will enure to the benefit of assignees who became such before the renewal, even if no assignment is made after the renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat non-English introductions the same as English inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: A manufacture, when first introduced into England (whether substance, machine, improvement, or combination of native discoveries), must be fully and correctly explained and is subject to the same laws and critical examination as if it were an English invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification requirements apply equally to foreign-origin inventions being patented in England.
